theme: Tesla and SpaceX open merger talks as AI credit risk hits new highs, chips sell off, and bitcoin treasury buying slows.

items.title: Cost to insure AI borrowers' debt (5-year CDS)
items.picked: A Bloomberg-sourced chart going viral on X says Oracle's 5-year CDS just topped 300bps, SpaceX passed 200bps and Meta hit a record 119bps as AI spending commitments pile up. This tab ranks those same names.
items.matters: CDS is what the market charges to insure a company's debt against default, so rising spreads mean lenders see the AI build-out as riskier. It also puts SpaceX in the same credit conversation as Oracle and the hyperscalers.
items.know: The sheet's levels are older snapshots quoted on X: Oracle 261bps (Oct 9), SpaceX 197bps (Oct 7), Broadcom 136bps (Oct 9), Meta 95bps, Nvidia 89bps, Amazon 73bps, Alphabet 72bps and Microsoft 52bps (Sep 28), against the IG index at 55bps. Today's quotes are higher, so treat the chart as the ranking, not the current level, and note CDS data is paywalled and dates differ.

items.title: SpaceX vs Tesla market value since the IPO
items.picked: Tesla and SpaceX both confirmed their boards formed special committees to look at deepening ties, including a possible combination, and Reuters says SpaceX approached Tesla about a merger. This chart shows how the two companies compare in size.
items.matters: In any deal, relative value sets who buys whom and the exchange ratio. The chart shows SpaceX has been worth more than Tesla every day since its IPO.
items.know: On Oct 20 the sheet has SpaceX at about $1,948B and Tesla at about $1,476B, a ratio of 1.32x, down from 1.51x on Oct 5 and back near its 1.32x on IPO day (Jun 12). The data stops Oct 20, so it misses Thursday's selloff when SPCX fell about 9%.

items.title: 30-day rolling correlation, TSLA vs SPCX
items.picked: With merger talk front and center, traders are treating SPCX and TSLA as a pair trade. This chart shows how tightly the two stocks have moved together.
items.matters: If the stocks already move as one, a combination changes less for holders, and a high correlation means owning both gives less diversification than people think.
items.know: The 30-day correlation was 0.58 on Oct 20 and 0.62 on Oct 19, up from roughly 0.05 to 0.09 in late July. Data ends Oct 20, before the merger headlines and Thursday's split move (TSLA about -3%, SPCX about -9%), which will pull the number down.

items.title: SpaceX after the IPO: drawdown and volatility vs Tesla
items.picked: Barchart's post that SPCX just had its third-worst day since listing is trending, with the stock down about 9% on Thursday. This chart tracks how far SPCX sits below its record close and how volatile it is next to Tesla.
items.matters: It shows the post-IPO ride has been rough even before the merger news, which matters for anyone sizing a position in either name.
items.know: On Oct 20 SPCX was 30.1% below its record close, with 10-day realized volatility of 33.8% vs Tesla's 30.8%. Drawdown peaked at about 31% in late September and SPCX vol hit 67.6% on Oct 15. Data ends Oct 20, so Thursday's drop isn't in it yet.

items.title: Tesla's active FSD subscriptions
items.picked: Sawyer Merritt's post that Tesla is adding a record 2,800 FSD subscribers a day, about $1.1B a year, is one of the biggest Tesla posts on X right now. This chart shows the reported subscriber count by quarter.
items.matters: FSD is the software revenue that bulls point to for robotaxi, and steady growth here supports the autonomy story in Tesla's valuation, including in any SpaceX deal talk.
items.know: Per Tesla's quarterly updates, active FSD subscriptions went from 0.95M in Q2 2025 to 1.74M in Q3 2026, up 67% in a year, with Q3 adding 0.26M. The count includes upfront purchases and monthly subs but excludes free trials, and the 2,800-a-day figure comes from the X post, not this sheet.

items.title: Quarterly capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle
items.picked: Meta fell about 7% after its earnings and posts on X are focused on its roughly $250B 2027 capex plan and first cash outflow in years. This chart shows how fast big tech capex has climbed.
items.matters: Capex at this pace is what's driving the AI credit-risk worries and the debt raises, so it ties together today's CDS, Meta and neocloud stories.
items.know: In the June 2026 quarter, Amazon spent $54.2B, Alphabet $44.9B, Microsoft $35.8B, Meta $30.1B and Oracle $16.5B, versus $32.2B, $22.5B, $17.1B, $16.5B and $9.1B a year earlier. The sheet stops at June 2026, so it doesn't include the September quarters now being reported.

items.title: Neocloud debt as % of market cap
items.picked: Nebius signed a $3.5B Citi credit facility for data centers and GPUs, yet its stock fell about 8.5%, and AI financing is the theme of the day. This chart compares how much debt each neocloud carries relative to its equity value.
items.matters: When debt approaches or exceeds market value, a stock drop makes leverage look worse fast and new funding gets pricier.
items.know: Using Oct 21 prices, Cipher's debt was 150% of its market cap, CoreWeave 116%, Applied Digital 101%, TeraWulf 82%, IREN 72% and Nebius 27% ($13.5B of debt on a $49.4B market cap). The Citi facility is undrawn and excluded, operating leases are excluded, and this is equity value, not enterprise value.

items.title: MSTR 30-day average daily trading volume
items.picked: BTCTreasuries' post that MSTR passed IBM in trading volume to become the 31st most-traded US stock is making the rounds. This chart shows MSTR's dollar volume trend.
items.matters: Heavy trading volume is what lets Strategy sell stock and preferreds through its ATM programs without crushing the price, so liquidity is part of the bitcoin-buying engine.
items.know: The 30-day average was about $3.26B a day as of Oct 16, with $4.35B traded that day, far below the spike shown around late 2024. The sheet ends Oct 16, and the IBM ranking comes from the X post, not this tab.

items.title: Strategy vs all other public companies' bitcoin
items.picked: Posts on X are claiming a Tesla-SpaceX combination would create a top corporate bitcoin holder, while Cointelegraph reports treasury companies are barely buying. This chart puts Strategy's pile next to everyone else's.
items.matters: It shows how concentrated corporate bitcoin is, so any new big holder, or Strategy slowing down, changes the picture.
items.know: As of Oct 14 the sheet has Strategy at 848,250 BTC and all other public companies at 455,468, so Strategy holds about 65% of the 1.30M total. Strategy added only about 2,250 BTC since Q2 while others added about 16,000. The Tesla and SpaceX bitcoin figures in the X posts aren't in this tab, and the universe is CoinGecko's list.

items.title: Software vs semiconductors
items.picked: The Nasdaq had its worst day since June and the SOX chip index dropped about 6.7% as the AI trade cracked. This chart tracks software stocks against chip stocks.
items.matters: Chips led the whole AI rally, so when semis fall harder than software the ratio swings back, which is a quick read on whether the market is rotating out of AI hardware.
items.know: Weekly data with Dec 2 2022 set to 100: on Oct 16 the software-to-semis ratio was 48.1, up from 41.9 on Oct 2, as SOXX fell from 476.7 to 399.3 while IGV was 192.0. The sheet ends Oct 16, so this week's chip selloff isn't in it yet.
